what: How close the Tier 1 neighbours are, and what that does to the value of a small gain

tier1-sp-sr.gap: +0.03334 = ONE clip crossing the gate, and it passes TWO teams

the_point: Every one of those is a small number. One clip crossing the 3 cm MP-SR gate is +1 rank; one clip crossing the 10 cm SP-SR gate is +2, because two teams are tied at 0.70. 0.86 cm of mean MPPE is +1, and 0.015 of AUC is +1. So up to +5 rank points sit within about one clip's worth of improvement -- not the 0.367 of AUC that separates us from first place, which is what I had been quoting as the Tier 1 story.

orientation_limited.e16: MPPE 2.91 cm and passes MP-SR at 30 deg, yet fails SP-SR at 0.5 rad = 28.6 deg, so its orientation error sits in that 1.4 deg band

why_the_warm_start_cannot_collect_it: 12 of 12 rejected Tier 1 clips came back WORSE on MPPE: e02 4.57 -> 35.05, e21 4.79 -> 10.34, e29 3.85 -> 8.72, e09 4.89 -> 11.66, e11 3.97 -> 4.44, e17 5.15 -> 5.29, e10 2.97 -> 6.13, e18 1.96 -> 4.39, e20 2.08 -> 3.10, e03 2.66 -> 2.80, e04 103 -> 122, and only e01 improved at all (43.67 -> 43.57). The arm trades position accuracy for reference tracking, which is the opposite of what a gate flip needs. So the remaining $2.61 cannot buy one of these, and that is a measurement, not a budget excuse.
what_this_changes_in_the_roadmap: The MP-SR item in docs/TO_THE_TOP.md was costed at ~$21 for 7 clips and valued at +7 rank points, which implicitly needed most of them to work. The board says ONE flip is worth +1 to +2, so the arm pays from its first success and does not need all seven. That makes a terminal-accuracy objective (tighter position and orientation in the final curriculum stage, or the contact-role reward in docs/ARM_CR.md) the best-value method work left, at roughly $3 per clip attempted.
